contracts.owner: Caller owns its candidate observations; no connection or FD acquired.

preconditions: Platform API requires USB host feature; application treats returned entries as observations.
postconditions: Returns a HashMap keyed by device name; does not authorize a selection or create a connection.
failure: Empty if no attached devices, host inactive/unsupported, or mService is null in this reference implementation.
RemoteException is rethrown from the system server; empty map is not the only failure outcome.

limitations: Map keys do not provide a cross-detach session identity.
Enumeration, permission check and open are separate observations, not one atomic transaction.

contracts.owner: System manages caller permission; application separately owns product run authorization.

preconditions: Use the candidate bound to the current application selection.
Applicable video-class clients targeting P or above additionally require CAMERA permission according to this API documentation.
postconditions: True reports current caller access; permission may come from temporary permission or a default-application association.
failure: mService null returns false.
RemoteException is rethrown from the system server.
Project rule: false or exception never grants acquisition admission.

limitations: True is not fresh Sidecar consent, continued permission, guaranteed open success, or RECORD_AUDIO authorization.

contracts.signature: public void requestPermission(UsbDevice device, PendingIntent pi)
contracts.owner: Caller creates and correlates PendingIntent; system delivers permission result.

preconditions: Project rule: register the outstanding nonce and selection/epoch/revision binding before invoking this API.
Applicable video-class/target-P CAMERA requirement remains in force.
postconditions: Return is void, not a permission decision.
A dialog may be displayed if permission was not already granted.
Granted temporary access lasts only until device disconnect.
failure: Permission result may be false.
RemoteException is rethrown; this does not create a grant.
Project rule: invocation failure invalidates the pending correlation rather than leaving it able to admit a late result.

limitations: This method forwards the supplied PendingIntent; its construction, matching identity, receiver exposure and flags are not implemented or audited here.

contains: public void requestPermission(UsbDevice device, PendingIntent pi)

contracts.owner: System populates documented extras; application owns interpretation and request correlation.

preconditions: A result must belong to a request the application still recognizes as outstanding. This is a project requirement.
postconditions: API promises the device passed into that request and a boolean permission decision.
failure: Project rule: missing/mismatched extras, false decision, stale nonce, old epoch/revision or duplicate consumption cannot open/start.

limitations: The extras do not contain an attachment epoch, application session, request nonce or authorization revision.
No guarantee here that the device remains attached at delivery, or that callbacks are ordered across requests/detach/reconnect.
A parcelled device object reference, deviceName or VID/PID cannot alone validate the current application session.

contains: containing the device passed into this call
permission was granted by the user

contracts.owner: Platform reports attachment events; application owns lifecycle epoch invalidation.

preconditions: Host attachment observations must be reconciled with the currently selected application binding.
postconditions: Documented attached and detached events contain EXTRA_DEVICE.
Project rule: disconnect invalidates the old epoch and outstanding permission request bindings; reconnect requires a new epoch and current permission/run authorization.
failure: Project rule: ambiguous identity or event ordering keeps admission closed; it cannot revalidate an old epoch.

limitations: The reference comments do not promise a never-reused deviceName, application epoch, global event ordering or no missed observation.
No automatic capture restart follows a reconnect or an old grant. These are project requirements, not added platform API behavior.

contracts.owner: Application allocates a unique owner for every successfully returned connection, including late results.

preconditions: Project rule: current explicit selection, attachment epoch and accepted system/product authorization must match.
Project rule: blocking platform work runs outside control/publication locks, on its designated worker.
postconditions: Implementation opens by device.getDeviceName(), creates a connection and closes the intermediate PFD.
Successful return provides a new connection resource; project revalidates its initiating binding before any borrow.
A stale successful return is cleaned up by its own owner and is never reassigned to a new session.
failure: Null PFD, unsuccessful connection.open or caught Exception result in null in this fixed implementation.
This is not a claim that every platform failure or Error is converted to null.

limitations: hasPermission true and a prior device list do not guarantee open success or eliminate detach races.
The API uses a name to reach the service; that does not turn the name into a durable session identity.

contracts.owner: Connection retains FD ownership; native receives only a borrow.

preconditions: Project rule: acquire an owner-bound borrow before reading/using FD, and prohibit owner close until accepted borrowers exit.
postconditions: Returns the native descriptor; documented unopened value is -1.
Getter does not duplicate the descriptor or transfer ownership in the normal Java-open path.
Project rule: reject negative results; integer 0 is not a failure sentinel.
failure: JNI returns -1 if its device context is absent.
usb_device_get_fd also returns -1 when reopening writable access fails.

limitations: getFileDescriptor directly invokes native_get_fd without the Java close mLock.
A nonnegative integer does not prove current authorization, attachment, transport readiness or a safe lifetime.
Generic usbhost getter calls reopen_writeable; do not generalize the normal Java-open path into an immutable integer for every backend path.

contains: -1 if the device is not opened.

contracts.owner: Intermediate PFD owns its original; connection owns the successful JNI duplicate; borrower owns neither.

preconditions: The service-provided PFD is passed to connection.open.
postconditions: JNI duplicates the PFD using F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC once during opening.
usb_device_new records the duplicate as device->fd and marks writeable=1 in the normal Java-open path.
UsbManager then closes its intermediate PFD copy.
failure: fcntl duplicate failure returns JNI_FALSE.
See framework-open-failure-boundary for overlapping cleanup sites on later failure; this contract does not certify every framework failure unwind.

limitations: getFileDescriptor is not another dup.
Project-selectable explicit dup would require a second distinct owner/cleanup policy and is not implemented or verified here.
Dup does not preserve authorization across detach, stop or revoke.

contracts.owner: Unique application connection owner invokes Java close; native borrower must not close the borrowed FD.

preconditions: Project rule: atomically reject new borrow first, then await all admitted native users and required driver drain evidence without holding control/publication locks.
postconditions: Reference Java implementation synchronizes mLock and invokes native_close only while open.
Native close invokes usb_device_close and clears the context; usb_device_close closes its held fd and frees the device.
Closed connection cannot be reused; communication requires a new openDevice result.
failure: Void return provides no structured I/O error, native transfer-drain receipt or application pixel-erasure receipt.
Project rule: unknown/failed or missing drain evidence remains pending; it cannot be converted into safe close by deadline alone.

limitations: Java repeated-close guard does not manage external native borrowers or independently duplicated descriptors.
Driver stopping, connection closure and Java-owned pixel zeroization are distinct obligations; inherit the protocol mapping rather than treating this method as the entire stop barrier.

contracts.signature: Project contract; no Android public method with this signature.
contracts.owner: Main integration owns selection_token, attachment_epoch, authorization_revision and permission_request_nonce.

preconditions: Bind a fresh single-use nonce to the current selection/epoch and request-time revision before requestPermission.
Design and verify a PendingIntent/receiver association that cannot mix requests; nonce in arbitrary extras is not by itself established proof.
postconditions: Consume only the matching current outstanding request once.
Recheck current candidate attachment observations and hasPermission before open; recheck the initiating identity after open returns.
Accepted authorization changes/revocation use monotone revisions; old results cannot restore current admission.
failure: Deny, missing extras, stale/duplicate/mismatched results or correlation ambiguity must not open/start.
Detach/stop/revoke invalidates outstanding correlation first; late results are ignored or clean up only their own returned resource.

limitations: These are proposed application fields, not fields guaranteed by UsbManager.
PendingIntent construction/matching, target-SDK mutability/flags and receiver-source/security enforcement were not available in the four selected inputs and remain separately required.
No atomicity is promised across callback, permission recheck and open.

contains: containing the device passed into this call

contracts.symbol: Sidecar connection owner and native borrow ledger
contracts.owner: One owner per connection; each admitted native operation holds an owner-bound borrow until its final use exits.

preconditions: Identity is an application owner/generation binding, never a lookup by FD number alone.
Register a borrow before getFileDescriptor/native entry; closing rejects new borrowers.
postconditions: Only the matching owner can release its connection after all admitted users and required native operations drain.
Old callbacks, same-number reused FDs and old permission/open results cannot close or mutate a newer owner.
Explicit duplicated descriptors, if later added, require independent acquisition/failure/close accounting.
failure: No response or uncertain native drain leaves owner and FD retained with admission revoked; it does not justify forced free or a false stopped acknowledgment.

limitations: This is not implemented by UsbDeviceConnection.mLock or the public getter.
VID/PID, deviceName, a UsbDevice object reference and integer FD are identifiers/observations, not complete session authorization.
No new PRD product state or test number is introduced by these internal contract fields.

contains: USB device name is the key

contracts.symbol: JNI open failure cleanup vs usb_device_new failure cleanup
contracts.signature: Static cross-file observation; not a new API or project implementation.
contracts.owner: Fixed framework/reference implementation has both visible close sites; project adds no speculative bare-FD cleanup.

preconditions: JNI calls usb_device_new with its newly duplicated descriptor.
postconditions: On null return JNI contains close(fd).
The callee failure label also contains close(fd) before returning NULL.
failure: This prevents certifying that every fixed framework open-failure path closes its descriptor exactly once.

limitations: No runtime reproduction, exploitability assessment, target-firmware claim or framework patch performed.
Normal successful-path connection ownership remains unchanged.
Do not compensate by closing a guessed/reused raw integer in application code.

replay.default: offline read-only; missing/mismatched input fails; no refresh or network fallback
